clue.text: Cleric's marks not getting better?

parts.note: a run of exam grades that slips from A down through B twice to E, never improving
the second grade in the declining run is a B
the grade stays at B, still no improvement
the run ends on a poor E grade

explanation.surface: A pupil's report card shows a clergyman's grades sliding steadily downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: The grades A, B, B, E read in order only fall or stay level, so the marks are indeed 'not getting better'. The 's is the definition's possessive read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French title for a priest or other ecclesiastic, so a cleric.

clue.text: Land's quickly covered by it

parts.note: a Land is a German federal state, and a fast German motorway lets drivers cover its territory quickly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' is not the countryside in general but a German state, like Bavaria; the capital L is the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, famous for its stretches without speed limits.

clue.text: Obstructions are mostly clogging pipes

indicators.note: one word blocks the inside of another, as dirt clogs a pipe

parts.note: briers are tobacco pipes made from brier root

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter lost

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Blockages are mostly what is clogging the plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: Brier pipes are carved from the root of the tree heath, hence the name; 'mostly' drops the last letter only.
explanation.definitionFit: Barriers are things that block the way, so obstructions.

clue.text: After release of clutch, reverses vehicles

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first, so the backing-up word follows

parts.note: a clutch is a nest of eggs, and its release is when the chicks hatch
to reverse a car is to back it, so reverses means backs

explanation.surface: A driver lets out the clutch pedal and backs the car up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' looks like the car pedal; here it is a brood of eggs, whose release is hatching.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatchbacks are cars with a rear door that opens upwards, a common class of vehicle.

clue.text: The men in the dock are not so confused

definitions.text: The men in the dock are not so
definitions.meaning: sailors whose ship is in dock are not out on the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: 'The dock' suggests a courtroom dock; here it is a harbour dock for ships.
explanation.definitionFit: At sea means both out on the ocean and bewildered.

clue.text: US university admitting one English or French author

indicators.note: the university lets the next letter in, taking it inside

parts.note: Cornell is an Ivy League university in New York State
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An American university admits a single English or French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Corneille was a seventeenth-century French dramatist, author of Le Cid.

clue.text: Bishop in power is not bad — hence approbation

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the preceding words are treated badly, their letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop holding power is no bad thing, so he earns approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not bad' reads as mild praise, but 'not' is part of the jumbled letters and 'bad' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownie points are credit for doing something that wins approval, especially from a superior.

clue.text: Work on last piece of paving

definitions.meaning: a last is a shoemaker's foot-shaped form, so working on it is mending shoes
a rounded stone set in a road surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' is not 'final' but the shoemaker's wooden foot model.
explanation.definitionFit: To cobble is to mend shoes, and a cobble is a rounded paving stone.

clue.text: Back after one

definitions.meaning: to support a motion or a candidate, as in 'I'll back that'
next in order after the first

explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it, and second follows first.

clue.text: Unexpected things found at the bottom of some bags

definitions.meaning: a turn-up for the books is a surprising event

definitions.text: found at the bottom of some bags

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is British slang for wide trousers (Oxford bags), not luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn-up is both a surprise and the folded cuff at a trouser bottom.

clue.text: Trouble for Scot in marriage, having means to get out

indicators.note: the Scots word sits inside the word for marriage

parts.note: a union is a marriage
fash is a Scots word meaning trouble or bother
able means having the means or capacity to do something

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's marital troubles are solved once he can afford to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: FASH is Scots dialect for bother, as in 'dinnae fash yersel'. 'Out' as the definition means no longer in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is out has gone out of style, no longer in vogue.

clue.text: Like diamonds of rich, randomly divided by disorderly mob

indicators.note: the first group is split apart by the second group placed in its middle
the word rich is rearranged at random into a new order
the word mob is put in disorder, its letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: A rich man's diamonds are seized by an unruly mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' looks like gems in a rich person's possession; here it is the shape, like the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is the diamond shape, so rhombic describes something shaped like diamonds.

clue.text: One transfers papers from French region following legal action

parts.note: Brie is a region east of Paris, famous for its cheese
f is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
a case is a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.surface: Someone carries documents from a region of France after a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is the bag in which one carries papers about, so it transfers them.

clue.text: Cover for leg that may be damaged by running

definitions.text: Cover for leg that may be damaged by running

parts.words: Cover for leg that may be damaged by running
parts.note: stockings made of a synthetic fibre ladder, or run, when snagged, so running here is a ladder spreading, not jogging

explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests an athlete's injured leg; a run is a ladder in a stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings, named for the synthetic fibre they are made of.

clue.text: Was forced to admit king is obliged to queen in emergency situation

indicators.note: the first word takes in, or admits, the next letter inside it

parts.note: had, as in 'had to go', means was forced
R is short for rex, Latin for king
should expresses obligation, as in 'you should go'
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A monarch is made to concede that he must bow to the queen in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'situation' as a place: the hard shoulder is the motorway strip where vehicles stop in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard shoulder is the roadside lane on British motorways reserved for stopping in an emergency.

clue.text: Worked too hard — it's clear cut

parts.note: overt means open and plain, clear to see
axed means cut, as with jobs or budgets

explanation.surface: Someone was overworked, and that is clear-cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear cut' looks like one adjective, meaning obvious; split it into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtaxed means strained by too heavy a burden, overburdened with work.

clue.text: Colleague in vehicle taking fish to wrong habitat

parts.note: the cod is a common sea fish
a river is fresh water, the wrong home for a sea fish like the cod

explanation.surface: A fellow passenger carries a fish to the wrong place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'wrong habitat' only makes sense relative to the fish: cod live in the sea, not a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-driver shares driving duties in a car, as in rallying, so a colleague in the vehicle.

clue.text: Where 14's situated, incidentally

definitions.meaning: the motorway emergency lane lies alongside the road
used to introduce a passing remark

explanation.walkthrough: Entry 14 is the motorway's emergency lane, which runs at the side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: By the way means both beside the road and as a passing aside.

clue.text: Balanced financial system that could make limited company money

parts.note: balanced in the sense of a blend of parts, as a varied diet is a mixed one

indicators.note: the letters of the answer's second word could be made from the next pieces, mixed together

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, as in a limited company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A balanced economic system is one in which a firm can turn a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is really a reverse clue: the answer's first word, read as an anagram signal, turns its second into CO (limited company) plus MONEY, which 'could make' points at.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an economy blending private enterprise with state ownership, a financial system of a particular kind.

clue.text: Casual work not even the most patient of men wanted

parts.note: odd numbers are not even
the biblical Job is proverbial for his patience

explanation.surface: Temporary work is not wanted even by the most long-suffering man.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd jobs are casual, occasional tasks done for pay.

clue.text: Puffer as part of train once

definitions.meaning: a railway carriage where passengers could formerly smoke

explanation.walkthrough: 'Puffer' suggests an old steam train, which fits the surface but is the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoker is a person who smokes and was once a carriage set aside for smoking.

clue.text: Bad spirit revealed by protest note

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or rally
N is short for note, as in a written note

explanation.surface: An evil spirit is unmasked by a protest message.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil supernatural being, a malevolent spirit.

clue.text: Position of maximum latitude, loyal to former PM

parts.note: true, as in a true friend, means loyal
Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence

explanation.surface: A loyal follower of an old prime minister holds a position far to the north.
explanation.definitionFit: True north is the direction of the geographic pole, where latitude reaches its maximum of ninety degrees.

clue.text: Covered by Thunderer's central section

indicators.note: the letters are taken from the middle part of the word, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: Something is covered by the central part of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunderer is the old nickname of The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Under means beneath, so covered by something above it.

clue.text: Music producer in what sounds like fist fight

indicators.note: the answer is said to resemble in sound the phrase that follows

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, as in 'put up your dukes'
to box is to fight with the fists

explanation.surface: A music machine sits in what seems like a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half changes sound: the slang word for a fist, with its first letter softened, plus the boxing word.
explanation.definitionFit: A jukebox is a coin-operated machine that plays chosen records, so it produces music.

clue.text: To deny support for West avoids trouble up front

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters go at the front, ahead of the compass letter
the word avoids is troubled, stirred up into a new order

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A Western ally refuses support to dodge trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support for' looks like part of the wordplay, but 'to deny support for' is the whole definition; 'up front' puts the jumble ahead of the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To disavow something is to disown or repudiate it, refusing to back it.

clue.text: They show skill, surrounded by lots of drinking

definitions.text: They show skill, surrounded by lots of drinking

indicators.note: the next word is enclosed within the word for drinking bouts

parts.note: benders are drinking sprees, so lots of drinking
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Barstaff display their craft while everyone around them is drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description: people whose craft is displayed while the drinking goes on around them, and the container spells exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartenders mix and serve drinks with flair in bars, surrounded by drinkers.

clue.text: Ravel's discordant interchange

definitions.meaning: to ravel or unravel cloth is to wear it into loose threads
a heated exchange or quarrel, a brawl

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the French composer; here it is the verb meaning to unravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Fray means both to wear into threads and a noisy fight or dispute.
